skill.name: protocol-reverse-engineering
skill.description: Guides authorized network protocol reverse engineering, including traffic capture, packet analysis, protocol dissection, and protocol documentation.
skill.summary: Analyze, document, and test network protocols from captured traffic.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples for packet filters, protocol signatures, Markdown paths, or binary protocol constants. Confirmed risks are sensitive TLS key material handling and dual-use interception, fuzzing, and replay guidance that needs clearer authorization and storage safeguards. No prompt injection evidence was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Active interception, fuzzing, and replay examples lack explicit authorization guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear rule that these steps must be used only on owned systems, lab targets, or systems with written permission.

remediation.issue: TLS key log examples store sensitive session secrets under /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Use a restricted-permission path, warn users to protect and delete key logs, and avoid shared temporary directories.

remediation.issue: Private key decryption guidance lacks handling warnings.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to load production private keys into analysis tools unless policy allows it and access is controlled.

content.value_statement: Protocol behavior is hard to understand from raw packet captures. This skill gives structured methods to capture, dissect, document, and test network protocols.
actual_capabilities: Guides packet capture workflows with Wireshark, tcpdump, tshark, mitmproxy, and Burp Suite.
Explains protocol identification using ports, banners, magic values, headers, and message patterns.
Shows how to parse binary message headers, TLV fields, length fields, and payload boundaries.
Provides TLS metadata, certificate, entropy, and decryption analysis techniques.
Helps produce protocol specifications, state machines, and Wireshark dissector outlines.
Includes examples for fuzzing, replay, and modified traffic testing in authorized labs.
limitations: It does not capture live traffic or inspect systems by itself.
It requires lawful authorization for interception, fuzzing, replay, and traffic modification.
Encrypted traffic analysis needs valid key logs, private keys, or other approved access.
Examples are templates and must be adapted to the target protocol and environment.

use_cases.title: Document a Proprietary Protocol
use_cases.description: Turn repeated packet captures into a clear message format, field map, and state machine.

use_cases.title: Debug Client and Server Traffic
use_cases.description: Use capture filters, stream following, and protocol signatures to find communication errors.

use_cases.title: Validate Parser Behavior
use_cases.description: Build controlled replay and fuzzing plans to test known protocol implementations.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Capture Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an authorized packet capture for a client and server protocol. Include tools, filters, files to collect, and safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Protocol Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these observed packet patterns and infer likely message boundaries, headers, length fields, message types, and session identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Protocol Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn my protocol observations into a concise specification with transport, message format, state machine, examples, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Authorized Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a lab-only fuzzing and replay plan for this protocol. Include scope limits, test cases, logging, rollback steps, and success criteria.

output_examples.input: A capture contains repeated TCP messages with a four-byte magic value, a version field, and changing payload lengths.
output_examples.output: A protocol outline that names the fixed header, maps probable field offsets, lists message types, and highlights unknown fields for more captures.

output_examples.input: A team needs to analyze encrypted traffic from its own test browser session.
output_examples.output: A safe workflow covering key log collection, restricted storage, Wireshark configuration, cleanup, and limits on production private key use.

output_examples.input: An implementation accepts custom binary messages and needs robustness testing in a lab.
output_examples.output: A scoped test plan with authorized targets, replay cases, boundary values, fuzzing priorities, monitoring steps, and stop conditions.

best_practices: Get written authorization before capturing, intercepting, fuzzing, replaying, or modifying traffic.
Store captures, TLS key logs, and private keys in restricted locations and delete them when analysis ends.
Validate protocol assumptions with multiple captures before writing parsers, dissectors, or test cases.
anti_patterns: Do not intercept third-party traffic or production users without explicit permission.
Do not place TLS key logs or private keys in shared temporary folders.
Do not run fuzzing or replay tests against live services without an approved change window.

faq.question: What does this skill help analyze?
faq.answer: It helps analyze network protocols from packet captures, binary payloads, TLS metadata, and repeated client-server behavior.

faq.question: Does it perform packet capture automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for tools such as Wireshark, tcpdump, tshark, Scapy, and mitmproxy.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe to use on any network?
faq.answer: No. Use it only on networks, systems, and traffic where you have clear legal authorization.

faq.question: Can it decrypt TLS traffic?
faq.answer: It can explain approved TLS analysis methods, but decryption requires valid key material or key logs that you are allowed to use.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare the scope, authorization, sample captures, target protocol details, tool versions, and storage rules for sensitive files.
